visible.title: st.file_uploader with accept_multiple_files=True leads to 400/502 errors sporadically (AWS deployment)
visible.body:
### Checklist

### Summary

We’re using a file upload widget with accept_multiple_files=True and sporadically getting either:
`Failed to load resource: the server responded with a status of 400 (Invalid session_id: <number here>)`
or
`Failed to load resource: the server responded with a status of 502 (Bad Gateway)`

while trying to upload several files (several being anything above ~10). Files are Fastq (.gz) files, the largest of which is ~85mb (our max file upload size is set to 200mb). Failures are sporadic but is seemingly dependent on the number of files uploaded. Not every file will fail, just a handful. 

The app is currently deployed to AWS as an auto-scaled and load-balanced ElasticBeanstalk application. We have tried enabling sticky sessions based on a similar issue here: [st.file_uploader returns HTTP code 400 with invalid session_id when deployed on Kubernetes · Issue #4173 · streamlit/streamlit · GitHub](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/4173) with no luck.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
selected_files = st.file_uploader("Select Fastq file pairs for upload:", help="Each pair must contain R1 + R2 files", type="gz", accept_multiple_files=True)
```

### Steps To Reproduce

### Expected Behavior

Ideally everything would upload and the user is free to proceed with the downstream analysis for these files. 

### Current Behavior

See summary for errors. 

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.13.0
- Python version: 3.10.8
- Deployed in an auto-scaled/auto-balanced AWS ElasticBeanstalk environment

### Additional Information

Issues that are not necessarily resolved that resemble this include:
https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/4173
https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/2803

### Are you willing to submit a PR?

- [ ] Yes, I am willing to submit a PR!

gold.summary: file_uploader multiple files -> sporadic 400 Invalid session_id / 502 on AWS deployment.

missing_info.item: Actual affinity cookie/routing for upload and WebSocket requests
missing_info.why: Verifies that the already-attempted sticky-session configuration is effective.

missing_info.item: Instance IDs/restarts and 400/502 LB logs at upload failure
missing_info.why: Separates cross-instance session loss from gateway/backend failure.

acceptable_next_steps: Acknowledge the attempted sticky sessions and verify upload/WebSocket requests reach the same live backend.
Compare a single-instance deployment and inspect failed upload/LB logs, including size/timeouts as hypotheses.
must_not: Simply repeat enable sticky sessions without acknowledging the previous attempt.
Treat 400 and 502 as proof of one identical root cause.
gold.reference: Maintainer: known issue with replicas; enable sticky sessions; closed as duplicate of #4173.
gold.review_reason: The visible report explicitly says sticky sessions were enabled with no luck. A similar multi-replica case is not proof of the same cause. Validate actual upload/WebSocket affinity, instance routing, restarts and LB logs before declaring the known limitation the full explanation.

acceptable_next_steps: Explain known multi-replica limitation; enable sticky sessions (cite #4173 / #2936 and architecture docs)
